verdict.rationale: Docs explicitly claim OCR works on low-quality and handwritten sources across 40+ languages, and multiple hands-on community reports (degraded 55-year-old paper files, handwritten forms) confirm strong real-world accuracy on messy scans. However other hands-on testers report concrete failures — one saw the OCR misclassify an entire page as an image, and another found a bidirectional Hebrew/English document produced output with no correspondence to the source text — directly contradicting the blanket accuracy claim in some real scenarios. Missing for 10: no documented handling of skewed pages or stamps specifically, no resolution/response to the reported failure cases, and no independent benchmark reconciling the mixed reports.
